title: DOIB: Distinct Objects, Identical Boxes (Stirling Numbers)
quickIdea: Splitting a set into unlabelled non-empty blocks. The count is the Stirling number of the second kind S(n,k).
remember: S(n,k) = number of ways to partition an n-set into k non-empty unlabelled blocks.
Empty boxes allowed: sum S(n,j) for j = 1..k, which is a Bell number when k = n.

example.work: The block containing 1 has 1, 2 or 3 partners: 1 + 3 + 3.

gateAngle: 'Set partition', 'groups of students', 'teams' with no names are all DOIB. The recurrence is the fastest hand computation when n and k are small.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: In how many ways can 4 distinct books be put into 2 identical bags, neither empty?
variations.why: Same as S(4,2). If the bags were distinct the answer would be 2! x 7 = 14.

trap.why: C(n,k) chooses k elements out of n; it does not partition anything. A partition into k blocks assigns every element to one of k unlabelled groups.
